title: Earl Bostic asks why he can't get a break
summary: Bostic visits Cobb after his spinal operation and asks why he never gets breaks; Cobb tells him people can't relate to so many notes and to play more melodically.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: You can't feel it in a lot of notes. I'm going to tell you -- I'm going to tell you a situation, something that -- I've got it on my lips, and I want to bring it up while we're talking about this, is technicians. Earl Bostick was a technician. Earl Bostick played a lot of notes. Earl Bostick, I told you, was responsible for my credit rating in New York through (inaudible). He vouched for me when my boss didn't vouch for me.

And when I had my spinal operation, he came up here and his wife came up to see me, and he said, come up for two reasons. I come up first to see you and see how you were doing, and then I want to ask you a question. He said, I know I'm a good musician. I know I know a lot of things to do. He said, but you come to town, Illinois Jacket come to town, Willis Jackson, Hal Sagle, everybody come to town and get a break, and I can't get a break, and I've been here, and I'm a good musician. What is wrong with me?

He asked me this. I said, Earl, I'm so glad you asked me. Now I can tell you because I didn't know what to say before. I says, you know one thing. You're not relating to people because they don't know about how many notes you play, and they can't follow it. And this when I went back
to tell (inaudible) I said, you remember Jimmie Lunceford -- would tell you what you do (inaudible) it's simple. The average public can relate to it. They can't relate to what you play.
I say, if you stay more melodic -- he say, well, I know melodies. He went to King Records, man, and everything he was playing was melodies.

And he forgot that fast playing, didn't he? He got it from me. He come to my house and asked me, and I'm laying flat on my back from a spinal operation, but he wanted to know what was wrong with him that he couldn't get a break. Everybody that come after him got a break, and he (inaudible).
Well, he did, you know, he was a hell of a player really.
